headline: Pilbara Minerals rockets nearly 10% today as lithium sentiment turns, gold hits all-time highs, and the RBA rate decision looms next week.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: PLS had a cracking session today, jumping 9.76% to $6.52. No single news catalyst has been confirmed, but lithium sentiment has been shifting — analysts are debating whether a supply deficit is building, and any positive read on that narrative tends to send Pilbara flying. Keep an eye on whether this holds or fades next week.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: GXAI.AX closed up nearly 3% today at $17.41. The AI infrastructure buildout story continues to attract attention — multiple articles today highlighted ASX-listed AI ETFs as well-positioned for the data centre spending boom. The GPT-5.6 release and intensifying AI price competition are keeping the sector hot.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG closed up 1.33% to $76.20, riding a strong day across the ASX. The broad market surged nearly 2% today, lifting this diversified ETF along with it. Solid, steady move — exactly what you'd expect from a high-growth multi-asset fund on a good market day.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market Shares ETF
movers.note: VTS.AX jumped 1.22% to $519.67 today. This ETF tracks the entire US share market, and it's benefiting from last night's S&P 500 and NASDAQ gains flowing through to the ASX-listed version. Strong US tech performance is the main engine here.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE.AX nudged up 0.46% to $91.32 today. Emerging markets had a mild positive session — no major specific catalyst, but the broadly risk-on tone in global markets gave it a gentle lift.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: GOOG edged up 0.45% to $358.16 in last night's session. No major company-specific news drove the move — it was a quiet, steady grind higher alongside the broader NASDAQ. Google remains well-placed in the AI race, though the spotlight has been on OpenAI's new GPT-5.6 release this week.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: MSFT barely moved last night, up just 0.10% to $390.74. Microsoft is still sitting below your average buy-in price, so the position is underwater. No fresh news today — it's largely treading water while the market waits for a new catalyst.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: TTWO dipped a tiny 0.16% last night to $211.75. The big news for Take-Two is positive though: GTA 6 now has a confirmed release date of November 19, 2026 for PS5 and Xbox. That date lock should be a meaningful catalyst — investors have been waiting on this for years.

movers.name: BetaShares Global Energy ETF
movers.note: FUEL.AX slipped 1.03% today to $8.63. WTI crude oil dropped over 3% last night to $84.88 a barrel — OPEC cut its 2026 demand growth forecast, which spooked oil markets. Lower oil prices directly drag on energy company earnings, and that's feeding straight into this ETF's price today.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX — Hold after a massive 9.76% day
watch_today.detail: Pilbara Minerals surged nearly 10% today to $6.52 — a huge single-session move. Analysts are divided on whether a real supply deficit is building in lithium, so this could be the start of a recovery or a short-term spike. You're still slightly underwater overall (-3.26%), so no need to rush. Hold and see if the momentum continues into next week before adding more.

watch_today.title: RBA rate decision next week — could move your whole portfolio
watch_today.detail: The RBA meets next week and the market is split on hold vs. hike. Westpac and several major banks are now forecasting rate cuts could begin soon, with some naming specific dates. A surprise hold or cut would be good news for growth assets like VDHG, GXAI, and property. A hike would sting. Watch for the decision and any press conference language carefully.

watch_today.title: TTWO — Hold, GTA 6 release date confirmed Nov 19
watch_today.detail: Take-Two officially has GTA 6 locked in for November 19, 2026 on PS5 and Xbox. This is the news the market has been waiting years for. The stock barely reacted last night (-0.16%), which likely means the market is still in 'wait and see' mode. As the date gets closer and pre-order/marketing buzz builds, expect more positive momentum. Hold your position.

watch_today.title: FUEL.AX — Watch oil weakness, consider your risk
watch_today.detail: WTI crude dropped over 3% last night to $84.88 after OPEC trimmed its 2026 demand growth forecast. FUEL.AX fell 1.03% today as a result. There's also a risk event looming — energy research firm Rystad has flagged a potential oil spike to $150 if Iran conflict escalates, but the base case right now is soft demand. FUEL is still marginally in the green overall. Hold, but watch oil prices closely this week.

watch_today.title: GXAI.AX — Momentum building on AI infrastructure theme
watch_today.detail: GXAI.AX jumped 2.96% today to $17.41. Multiple outlets today called out AI ETFs as well-positioned for the data centre buildout boom, and OpenAI's GPT-5.6 launch is sparking a broader AI spending story. Still down 8.51% overall, but the thesis is tracking. Hold and let the AI cycle do the work.

watch_today.title: Gold hits $4,215 USD/oz — all-time high territory
watch_today.detail: Gold surged over 3% last night to $4,215/oz. This kind of spike often signals that big investors are nervous about something — whether it's geopolitical risk, inflation fears, or uncertainty around central bank moves. It's a yellow flag for risk assets broadly. Nothing to panic about, but worth noting if you're thinking about adding to growth positions right now.

markets.summary: The ASX had a cracking day — the ASX 200 closed up nearly 2% at 8,804, its biggest single-day gain in a while. Locally, the mood was boosted by growing expectations the RBA is done raising rates. Last night in the US, the S&P 500 rose 0.5% to 7,431 and the NASDAQ edged up 0.31% to 25,888 — solid but not spectacular. The big stories in commodities: gold smashed through to $4,215/oz (up 3%), and oil took a beating, falling 3.2% to $84.88 after OPEC cut its demand forecast. The Aussie dollar was essentially flat at 70.49 US cents.

politics.summary: All eyes are on the RBA's meeting next week, with banks now publicly naming dates for rate cuts. Meanwhile, Labor is facing scrutiny over economic management, a proposed human rights law is back on the table, and a controversial corporate tax rate is making headlines.

stories.title: Big banks name dates for interest rate cuts — relief coming for home owners
stories.why_it_matters: Several of Australia's major banks have now publicly named specific dates for when they expect the RBA to start cutting interest rates, described as 'welcome relief' for home owners. The AFR also reports the RBA is seen as done raising rates, with housing facing 'tax headwinds' from banks. If cuts arrive as expected, that's directly good news for mortgage holders on the Gold Coast — and good for growth assets like VDHG in your portfolio. The RBA meeting is next week, so this is front and centre.

stories.title: Westpac forecasts RBA's next move — hold or hike?
stories.why_it_matters: Westpac has weighed in on what the RBA will do at next week's meeting. The debate is whether the Reserve Bank holds the cash rate steady or delivers a surprise hike. The broader market consensus is leaning toward a hold, with cuts expected later in 2026. For anyone with a mortgage or growth investments, a hold is the neutral outcome — but a cut would send asset prices higher.

stories.title: Labor considers landmark human rights law — again
stories.why_it_matters: The Albanese government is again considering introducing a national Human Rights Act — a move that's been floated several times but never delivered. Such a law would give Australians the ability to challenge government decisions that breach rights like privacy, equality, and fair treatment. It's a significant piece of legislation if it proceeds, but has historically stalled due to political complexity. No firm timeline has been announced.

stories.title: Australia's 55% tax on retained profits — second highest in the world
stories.why_it_matters: The AFR reports that Australia's effective tax rate on retained business profits — where a company keeps earnings rather than paying them out as dividends — sits at 55%, the second highest in the world. This is a combination of corporate tax and the dividend imputation system (the franking credits setup). Critics say it discourages businesses from reinvesting profits, which could weigh on long-term economic growth. It's a live debate as the government faces pressure over economic management.

ai.summary: The big AI story this week is OpenAI's GPT-5.6 launch sparking a full-on price war between the major AI companies. Regulation is also heating up globally, with Canada moving to control AI chatbots and US legal scholars debating property rights in the age of AI.

stories.title: GPT-5.6 launch triggers AI price war — good news for users
stories.why_it_matters: OpenAI has released GPT-5.6, and the move is forcing competing AI companies — Google (Gemini), Anthropic (Claude), and others — to slash their prices to stay competitive. Gizmodo has already published a breakdown comparing the real cost of using Claude, GPT-5.5, and Gemini 3.5 Flash. For everyday users, this is great news — AI tools are getting cheaper and more capable fast. For investors in GOOG (Alphabet/Gemini) and MSFT (which backs OpenAI), the price war squeezes margins but keeps both companies fighting hard for market share.

stories.title: Marc Andreessen blasts AI regulation after Anthropic model shutdown
stories.why_it_matters: Prominent tech investor Marc Andreessen has publicly criticised the AI regulation debate after Anthropic was reportedly forced to shut down one of its AI models due to regulatory pressure. Andreessen argues that heavy-handed regulation stifles innovation and that governments are too slow to understand what they're trying to control. This is a key tension playing out globally — the US, Canada, and EU are all moving toward AI rules, but the industry is pushing back hard. For GOOG and MSFT investors, regulatory risk is a real factor to watch.

stories.title: Canada moves to regulate social media and AI chatbots
stories.why_it_matters: Canada is pushing ahead with legislation to regulate both social media platforms and AI chatbots — meaning companies like Google and Microsoft could face new compliance rules in a major Western market. The laws would likely require AI chatbots to be more transparent about their outputs and limit certain uses on social platforms. This adds to a growing global patchwork of AI rules that big tech companies will need to navigate. More compliance costs, but also potentially less competition from smaller players who can't afford to comply.

stories.title: AI infrastructure boom: ASX ETFs gaining attention for data centre play
stories.why_it_matters: Multiple Australian finance outlets today highlighted ASX-listed AI ETFs — including GXAI.AX — as well positioned to benefit from the massive global data centre spending boom. Tech giants are pouring hundreds of billions into AI infrastructure (chips, power, cooling, servers), and ETFs that hold companies across this supply chain stand to benefit. GXAI.AX is one of those named — relevant directly to your portfolio, and it showed today with a near-3% gain.

sport.summary: The Dolphins are on fire in the NRL, the Broncos got smashed by the Bunnies, and the Tigers are dealing with a big injury headache ahead of Sunday's game. In AFL, Geelong put on a clinic against the Gold Coast Suns.

stories.title: Dolphins thrash Roosters 48-10, win six in a row
stories.why_it_matters: The Dolphins demolished the Sydney Roosters 48-10 at Suncorp Stadium on Friday night, notching their sixth consecutive win. That's a red-hot run of form for the Queensland club. The Roosters were completely outclassed — a 38-point margin is a thumping by any measure. The Dolphins are making a serious charge up the NRL ladder heading into the business end of the season.

stories.title: Rabbitohs belt Broncos 48-6 — Brisbane's woes deepen
stories.why_it_matters: South Sydney put on a clinic Thursday night, belting Brisbane 48-6 at Accor Stadium. A 42-point loss for the Broncos is a disaster — it's the kind of result that raises real questions about where Brisbane is headed this season. The Rabbitohs, meanwhile, look like a serious contender with that sort of firepower on display.

stories.title: Wests Tigers lose enforcer for season; Sharks make shock dual switch ahead of Round 15
stories.why_it_matters: Wests Tigers coach Benji Marshall has lost a key enforcer for the rest of the season ahead of Sunday's home game against the Gold Coast Titans at Leichhardt Oval. The Sharks have also made a surprise dual positional switch heading into Saturday's clash with the Warriors in Auckland. A young Tigers debutant is set to come in, adding intrigue to the Titans game — good news for Gold Coast fans watching Sunday.

stories.title: Geelong smash Gold Coast Suns in AFL — 'Big Max' starring at the 'G
stories.why_it_matters: Geelong put on a dominant AFL display, thumping the Gold Coast Suns in a match that was never really in doubt. Max Holmes (known as 'Big Max') was the star, getting the MCG crowd rocking early. It's a tough result for the Suns, who are the local team for Gold Coast footy fans. Geelong's forward line looked devastating — not great news if you're backing the Suns to push into finals contention this year.
